daily_sets.focus: Breadth pass — touch every category once and find your slow commands.
Weak-area hammering — AD cmdlets and network triage until they are automatic.
Confidence builder — the 20 highest-yield commands. Clean reps only, no peeking.

error_recovery.error_output:
Get-ADUser : A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'eq'.
At line:1 char:24
+ Get-ADUser -Filter Name -eq "jdoe"
+                        ~~~
error_recovery.explanation: -Filter accepts exactly one string. Without quotes, PowerShell tokenizes Name -eq "jdoe" into separate arguments, so -eq looks like a brand-new parameter — and no cmdlet has an -eq parameter. Wrapping the whole expression in single quotes hands -Filter a single string, which the AD provider then parses as its own filter language (the double quotes survive inside to delimit the value).

error_recovery.error_output: New-ADUser : Cannot bind parameter 'AccountPassword'. Cannot convert value "P@ssw0rd!" to type "System.Security.SecureString".
error_recovery.explanation: -AccountPassword is typed as SecureString, and PowerShell refuses to auto-convert a plain string into one. That is a deliberate safety rail: a plain string would sit in memory as readable text, while a SecureString keeps the secret encrypted in memory. Read-Host -AsSecureString (or ConvertTo-SecureString) builds the SecureString the parameter demands.

error_recovery.error_output: Add-ADGroupMember : A positional parameter cannot be found that accepts argument 'jdoe'.
error_recovery.explanation: Only -Identity accepts positional input on this cmdlet. The second bare string has no parameter left to bind to, so the parameter binder throws. Naming both parameters explicitly removes the ambiguity — -Identity takes the group, -Members takes the user.

error_recovery.error_output:
cmdlet Set-ADAccountPassword at command pipeline position 1
Supply values for the following parameters:
OldPassword: ********
error_recovery.explanation: Without -Reset you are performing a user-initiated password CHANGE, which proves identity by demanding the old password first — hence the surprise OldPassword prompt. -Reset switches the operation to an administrative reset, the help-desk override path that does not need the old secret. Forgetting -Reset is the classic reason a 'password reset' stalls mid-script.

error_recovery.error_output:
'traceroute' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
error_recovery.explanation: traceroute is the Linux/macOS name for the tool. Windows ships the same utility under the 8.3-era name tracert. Muscle memory carried over from a Linux lab dies instantly on a Windows assessment box — train the Windows spelling so your fingers don't betray you.

error_recovery.error_output: Ping request could not find host 10.0.1.256. Please check the name and try again.
error_recovery.explanation: Each IPv4 octet maxes out at 255, so 10.0.1.256 is not an address at all. Windows then treats the token as a hostname and attempts DNS resolution, which fails. The error looks like a name-resolution problem, but the root cause is an impossible octet — always sanity-check the numbers before chasing DNS.

error_recovery.error_output: Where-Object : A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'eq'.
error_recovery.explanation: -FilterScript takes exactly one scriptblock. Without braces, PowerShell evaluates $_.Status as a loose expression (worth $null outside any pipeline context) and then trips over -eq as a stray would-be parameter. The braces package the whole comparison into a single scriptblock that Where-Object executes once per piped object, with $_ bound to the current one.

IOS is a mode hierarchy: user EXEC mode only runs informational commands like show and ping. configure terminal lives in privileged EXEC mode, so the parser rejects it at the very first character. enable escalates you to privileged mode — only then does the configuration parser even exist. If a config command is rejected instantly, you are almost certainly in the wrong mode.

error_recovery.broken_command: BACKUP DATABASE [SalesDB] TO DISK = 'E:\Backups\SalesDB_full.bak' WITH INIT;
error_recovery.error_output:
Msg 3201, Level 16, State 1, Line 1
Cannot open backup device 'E:\Backups\SalesDB_full.bak'. Operating system error 3(The system cannot find the path specified.).
error_recovery.explanation: SQL Server will open the backup file but it never creates directories — the target folder must already exist on the server. OS error 3 means the PATH is missing, not the file. Create E:\Backups first (New-Item -ItemType Directory), then re-run the BACKUP. This is the number-one reason a backup step fails under time pressure.

error_recovery.broken_command: RESTORE DATABASE [SalesDB] FROM DISK = 'E:\Backups\SalesDB_full.bak' WITH RECOVERY;
error_recovery.error_output:
Msg 3101, Level 16, State 1, Line 1
Exclusive access could not be obtained because the database is in use.
error_recovery.explanation: A restore needs an exclusive lock on the database, and any live user connection blocks it. SET SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE force-rolls-back every open transaction and disconnects the other sessions, freeing the lock the restore requires. Run the ALTER first, then the RESTORE — and warn the room before you boot everyone's sessions.
error_recovery.fix: ALTER DATABASE [SalesDB] SET SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE;

error_recovery.error_output: Add-DhcpServerv4Scope : The start range address is greater than the end range address.
error_recovery.explanation: The cmdlet validates start <= end before it touches anything — a lease pool cannot grow backwards. Under time pressure it is easy to type the range high-to-low. Swap the two addresses and the validation passes.

error_recovery.error_output:
DISKPART> list disks

The arguments specified for this command are not valid.

For more information on the command type: HELP LIST
error_recovery.explanation: diskpart's LIST subcommand takes singular object names — disk, volume, partition — because it lists instances of one object type at a time. 'disks' matches no grammar rule, so the parser rejects it. Keep every diskpart noun singular: list disk, select disk 0, list volume.
